text:
Tyler Boucher waited a long time for this. The Senators took him 10th overall in 2021, and five years and a full AHL season later he got his NHL debut in Winnipeg and scored on his first shot, a wrist shot 4:04 into the second period that made it 2-0. Graeme Nichols of Coming Down the Pipe noted that only Carter Yakemchuk had done that before among Ottawa first-rounders debuting for the club. Boucher played 6:12. It was enough.

The goal that mattered more was the win itself, because the Senators spent the night proving the 2-1 score flattered the Jets. Ottawa had 4.54 expected goals (the quality of its chances) to Winnipeg's 2.01 and won every period on chances, starting with a 1.69 to 0.74 first. By our replays of every shot, Ottawa wins this game 80% of the time. Tim Stützle was on the ice for 3.23 expected goals for in 21 minutes and Jake Sanderson for 2.80 in nearly 25, which is what driving play looks like.

Stuart Skinner is why it stayed close. The Jets' goalie stopped Jordan Spence on a 37% chance in the first and finished 1.9 goals better than the 27 shots he faced deserved, the most wins added of anyone on the ice. Drake Batherson finally beat him on the power play at 3:06 of the second, and Boucher followed 58 seconds later. Viggo Björck, the Jets' eighth overall pick this summer, answered with his own first NHL goal at 9:24, a nice moment on a night that otherwise belonged to the visitors. Linus Ullmark took it from there, 20 saves on 21 shots and a big stop on Kyle Connor.

Winnipeg's six-game winning streak is over, though the Jets, rebuilt on the fly after the Hellebuyck trade and riding Mark Scheifele's record-book week, have little to apologise for in November. Ottawa has won three straight, and this one was earned.
headline: Boucher scores in his debut as Ottawa snaps the Jets' streak
